body:
INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY REVIEW of cand-0BZ23034MFEENEZ7RQYCRB8NJK, exact 459640df448695. Assigned by
the chief; I am NOT the required formal reviewer (that is scout) and I have reserved nothing and
edited nothing. One substantive finding, and it is a precondition rather than a defect.

SCOPE VERIFIED MYSELF, not taken from the proposal:
  parents of 459640df                     1 (sole parent)
  base                                    e584ad6, matching the row
  paths in diff                           1, docs/design/external-floor-calibration-court.md
  455 lines, twelve sections

WHAT I CHECKED AGAINST SOURCE RATHER THAN READING:

  §5 Unranked semantics. "the aligner could not rank the unit: semantic providers abstained and no
  other channel supplied ranking evidence." Confirmed against hsmm.scala:593 - the Unranked state is
  taken only when `set.abstained && set.ranked.isEmpty` - and CandidateSet's own docstring, which
  defines `abstained` as no ranking evidence existing at all.

  §6 collapse rule. "any external state except Unranked is predicted external" maps EXACTLY onto
  AlignState.externals, which is `ExternalState.values.filterNot(_ == Unranked).map(External(_))` at
  matrix.scala:64. The document's partition and the code's partition are the same partition, which
  is the kind of agreement that is easy to assume and worth confirming.

  §5 support gate. The court says an empty eligible denominator cannot publish 1.0 and that external
  content support is not-applicable or separately typed. That is correct and it is exactly the state
  of the code: hsmm.scala:597 builds every external row with four positional arguments, so it carries
  terms EMPTY with supportWeight 1.0. In the WOG golden, 10 of 18 breakdowns are that shape and ZERO
  rows with non-empty terms carry 1.0. THE AUTHOR HAS ALREADY GATED ON THIS - "no execution may pass
  the court until that repair lands" - which answers the dependency I raised pre-review. Nothing owed
  to me here.

  §3 nomination-provenance precondition. It enumerates channel, channel-local rank, raw score with
  declared direction, feature space, provider/geometry, hierarchy stratum, and derivation receipt -
  the same coordinates frozen in bd-01M1CBKNA3KTBYTB3BACXJMXZZ - and refuses a reusable floor until
  that residual closes. The two documents agree without having been written together.

THE FINDING - §5 FREEZES A SEMANTIC CLAIM THAT ONE CODE PATH CAN FALSIFY, AND THE COURT NEVER NAMES
THAT PATH.

  §5: Unranked "is an aligner support failure. It never means that a participant intruded,
  associated, inferred, or produced uninterpretable content."

  candidates.scala:38-40:
    def without(channel: String): CandidateSet =
      val kept = nominations.filterNot(_.channel == channel)
      CandidateSet(kept, abstained = abstained || (kept.isEmpty && nominations.nonEmpty))

  So an ABLATION that empties a candidate set sets `abstained`, which routes the unit to Unranked -
  a state the court defines as provider abstention. The experiment becomes an alleged aligner
  failure.

  WHY THIS IS NOT A BLOCK AS WRITTEN: §8's controls are INDEPENDENT RUNS - hashed n-gram and TF-IDF,
  each with its own geometry identity, floor grid and inference runs - not `without()` ablations of a
  combined set. I checked; the word ablation does not appear in the document. So the conflation does
  not bite this court today.

  WHY IT IS STILL WORTH ONE SENTENCE: this document is meant to be immutable and to FREEZE meanings.
  It freezes "Unranked never means X" while a public method one module over can produce Unranked from
  a channel manipulation. A future execution that compares channels with `without()` instead of
  separate runs would make §5 false without touching §5. Naming the precondition - executions
  establish channel comparisons by independent runs, not by `CandidateSet.without` - costs a line and
  closes it.

  CORROBORATION: this is the same conflation the chief raised independently as AMEND item 3 on my
  nomination court two hours ago. Two documents, two reviewers, one code path. That raises my
  confidence it is real rather than my own hobby-horse.

WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY, stated so nobody credits me with it: §§4, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12 I read but did
not independently reproduce. The nested macro-averaging in §6 I checked for internal consistency and
against the code's state partition, NOT for statistical adequacy - whether participant-level equal
authority is the right estimand for this population is a question I am not qualified to settle and
scout is the right reviewer for it. My competence here is the align semantics and the source
correspondence, and that is what I checked.

VERDICT: strong document; I would AMEND for the one §5 precondition sentence rather than block, and I
would not hold it for anything else I found.
